en.B: In the first month the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, the whole congregation, arrived in the wilderness of Zin, and the people settled at Kadesh. Miriam died there, and there she was buried.

vi.B: Vào tháng thứ nhất, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, tức là toàn thể hội chúng, đến hoang mạc Xin, và dân chúng ở lại Ca-đe. Mi-ri-am qua đời tại đó và được chôn cất tại đó.
vi.R: Vào tháng đầu tiên trong năm, toàn thể cộng đồng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đến hoang mạc Xin. Dân chúng ở lại Ca-đe. Mi-ri-am qua đời và được chôn cất tại đó.

decisions.choice: the first month: the year is not stated
alternatives: the first month of the third year, soon after the events of chapters 13-14
decisions.reason: The verse names the month but not the year. Aaron dies later in this chapter (verses 22-29), and 33:38 dates his death to the fifth month of the fortieth year after the exodus. So this arrival at Kadesh is most likely in the first month of the fortieth year, near the end of the wilderness years, while the earlier stay at Kadesh (13:26) came in the second year. The text does not say this directly.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Zin and Kadesh: on the southern edge of Canaan
decisions.reason: The wilderness of Zin lay along the southern border of the promised land (34:3-4). Kadesh, also called Kadesh-barnea (32:8), is where the spies returned to the people (13:26, which places it in the wilderness of Paran; the two wilderness areas met near it). It is named with Zin again in 33:36. From here Israel will try to go on toward the land (verse 14).

decisions.choice: Miriam died: the first of the three leaders to die
decisions.reason: Miriam was the sister of Moses and Aaron (26:59; Exodus 15:20). She dies at Kadesh; Aaron dies later in this chapter (verse 28), and Moses learns here that he too will not enter the land (verse 12). Her death and burial are recorded, but no mourning is described, unlike Aaron's (verse 29).

decisions.choice: the first month of the year / the Zin Desert
decisions.reason: Readable adds "of the year" so that the reader knows a month of the calendar is meant, and calls the wilderness a desert, as elsewhere at this level.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("arrivèrent", "mourut"); passé composé at Readable ("est arrivée", "est morte")
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Pentateuch: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé that of spoken and school French.

en.B: There was no water for the congregation, and they gathered together against Moses and Aaron.
en.R: The community had no water. So the people came together as a crowd and turned against Moses and Aaron.

es.R: La comunidad no tenía agua. Por eso la gente se reunió en masa y se puso en contra de Moisés y Aarón.

fr.R: La communauté n’avait pas d’eau. Alors les gens se sont rassemblés en foule et se sont tournés contre Moïse et Aaron.

vi.B: Hội chúng không có nước, nên họ kéo nhau đến chống lại Môi-se và A-rôn.
vi.R: Cộng đồng không có nước uống. Vì vậy dân chúng tụ tập thành một đám đông và quay sang chống lại Môi-se và A-rôn.

decisions.choice: no water: the same test as at Rephidim
decisions.reason: The scene recalls Exodus 17:1-7, where the people had no water at Rephidim, quarreled with Moses, and the place was named Meribah. Near the end of the wilderness years the people face the same lack, and they respond in the same way.

decisions.choice: assembled against: gathered as a hostile crowd
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for gathering an assembly. With "against" it describes a crowd that comes together to oppose someone, as Korah's company did against Moses and Aaron (16:3; 17:7).

decisions.choice: came together as a crowd and turned against
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that the gathering was hostile, which is what "assembled against" means.

en.B: The people argued with Moses. "We wish we had died," they said, "when our {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} perished before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.R: They argued with Moses and said, "We wish we had died with our {{gender:relatives|brothers}} when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} punished them!

sw.R: Walibishana na Musa, wakasema, "Heri tungalikufa pamoja na ndugu zetu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipowaadhibu!

vi.B: Dân chúng cãi vã với Môi-se. Họ nói: "Phải chi chúng tôi đã chết khi anh em chúng tôi bỏ mạng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}!

decisions.choice: quarreled: argued, brought a complaint against
decisions.reason: The verb (riv) means to argue or to bring a case against someone. It gives the place its name, Meribah, "quarreling" (verse 13), as at Exodus 17:2, 7.

decisions.choice: when our brothers died before the LORD: those who died after Korah's rebellion
decisions.reason: The people mean the deaths that followed Korah's rebellion: those whom the earth swallowed and the fire consumed (16:31-35), and the 14,700 who died in the plague (17:14). They died "before the LORD", struck down in the LORD's presence as a judgment. The people say they would rather have died then than die slowly of thirst.

decisions.choice: if only we had died: a wish about the past
decisions.reason: The small word that opens the cry expresses a wish that can no longer come true, as in 14:2.

decisions.choice: our brothers: our fellow Israelites, women as well as men
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow members of the people. Those who died in chapters 16-17 included whole households (16:27, 32) and the many who died in the plague.

decisions.choice: when the LORD punished them
decisions.reason: "Died before the LORD" refers to deaths that were the LORD's judgment (chapters 16-17). Readable says so plainly.

decisions.choice: ndugu zetu
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already includes women and men and is the ordinary word for fellow members of a people, so the Swahili needs no gender span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: The people speak to Moses as "ông" (to Moses and Aaron together "các ông") and call themselves "chúng tôi"
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet: respectful but not courtly; the complaint stays a complaint. "anh em chúng tôi" (B) and "bà con chúng tôi" (R) include women and men, so no gender span is needed.

en.R: Why did you bring the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} out into this desert? Do you want us and our animals to die here?

vi.B: Tại sao các ông đem hội của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} vào hoang mạc này, để chúng tôi và súc vật chúng tôi phải chết ở đây?

decisions.choice: the assembly of the LORD: the people as the LORD's own
decisions.reason: The people call themselves the LORD's assembly, the phrase Korah used against Moses (16:3). They claim that, as the LORD's people, they deserve better than to die in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: why have you brought: an accusation, not a request for a reason
decisions.reason: The question blames Moses and Aaron ("you" is plural) for the journey; it does not expect an answer.

decisions.choice: Do you want us and our animals to die here?
decisions.reason: Readable makes the purpose clause into a second question, which carries the same accusation in shorter sentences.

records.literal_gloss: And why did you bring us up from Egypt, to bring us to the place the evil the this? Not [a] place of seed and fig and vine and pomegranate, and water there is not to drink.

en.L: And why did you bring us up from Egypt, to bring us to this evil place? [It is] not a place of seed or fig or vine or pomegranate, and there is no water to drink."
en.B: Why did you bring us up out of Egypt only to lead us into this terrible place? Nothing can be sown here, and there are no figs, no vines, no pomegranates, and there is not even water to drink!"
en.R: Why did you make us leave Egypt and bring us to this awful place? We cannot plant grain here. There are no figs, grapevines or pomegranates. There is not even any water to drink!"

es.L: ¿Y por qué nos {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} subir de Egipto, para traernos a este lugar malo? No [es] lugar de sementera, ni de higuera, ni de vid, ni de granado, y no hay agua para beber».

es.R: ¿Por qué nos {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} salir de Egipto y nos {{plural_you:trajeron|trajisteis}} a este lugar horrible? Aquí no podemos sembrar grano. No hay higueras, ni parras, ni granados. ¡Ni siquiera hay agua para beber!».

fr.L: Et pourquoi nous avez-vous fait monter d’Égypte, pour nous amener dans ce mauvais lieu ? [Ce n’est] pas un lieu de semence, ni de figuier, ni de vigne, ni de grenadier, et il n’y a pas d’eau à boire. »

fr.R: Pourquoi nous avez-vous fait quitter l’Égypte pour nous amener dans cet endroit horrible ? Nous ne pouvons pas y planter de céréales. Il n’y a pas de figuiers, pas de vignes, pas de grenadiers. Il n’y a même pas d’eau à boire ! »

vi.L: Và tại sao các ông đã đem chúng tôi lên khỏi Ai Cập, để đem chúng tôi đến nơi tồi tệ này? [Đây] không phải là nơi có hạt giống, cây vả, cây nho hay cây lựu, và cũng không có nước để uống."

decisions.choice: evil place: a bad, miserable place
decisions.reason: "Evil" here means bad or harsh, not morally wicked: a place where nothing grows and there is no water.

decisions.choice: seed, fig, vine, pomegranate: what the promised land would give
decisions.reason: The spies brought back grapes, pomegranates and figs from the land (13:23). The people now complain that they have none of what that land offered. "Seed" means grain that is sown.

decisions.choice: Nothing can be sown here / We cannot plant grain here
decisions.reason: "Not a place of seed" means a place where crops cannot be sown. Balanced and Readable say that, and Readable names grain.

en.R: Moses and Aaron left the crowd and went to the entrance of the meeting tent. They bowed down with their faces to the ground. Then the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to them.

es.L: Y fueron Moisés y Aarón de delante de la asamblea a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro, y cayeron sobre sus rostros, y la gloria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se les apareció.
es.B: Moisés y Aarón se apartaron de la asamblea y fueron a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro. Se postraron rostro en tierra, y la gloria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se les apareció.
es.R: Moisés y Aarón se alejaron de la multitud y fueron a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro. Se inclinaron con la cara hasta el suelo. Entonces la gloria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se les apareció.

fr.L: Et Moïse et Aaron allèrent de devant l’assemblée à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre, et ils tombèrent sur leur face, et la gloire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} leur apparut.
fr.B: Moïse et Aaron quittèrent l’assemblée et allèrent à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre. Ils se jetèrent face contre terre, et la gloire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} leur apparut.
fr.R: Moïse et Aaron ont quitté la foule et sont allés à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre. Ils se sont prosternés, le visage contre le sol. Alors la gloire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} leur est apparue.

sw.L: Nao Musa na Haruni wakaenda kutoka mbele ya kusanyiko mpaka mlango wa Hema la Kukutania, wakaanguka kifudifudi, na utukufu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukawatokea.
sw.B: Musa na Haruni waliondoka mbele ya kusanyiko wakaenda mlangoni pa Hema la Kukutania. Wakaanguka kifudifudi, na utukufu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukawatokea.
sw.R: Musa na Haruni waliuacha umati wakaenda mlangoni pa Hema la Kukutania. Wakasujudu, nyuso zao zikigusa ardhi. Kisha utukufu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukawatokea.

vi.L: Và Môi-se và A-rôn đi khỏi trước mặt hội đến cửa Lều Hội Kiến, và họ sấp mặt xuống, và vinh quang của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với họ.
vi.B: Môi-se và A-rôn rời khỏi hội chúng, đi đến cửa Lều Hội Kiến. Họ sấp mặt xuống đất, và vinh quang của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với họ.
vi.R: Môi-se và A-rôn rời đám đông và đi đến cửa Lều Hội Kiến. Họ cúi sấp mặt xuống đất. Rồi vinh quang của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với họ.

decisions.choice: fell on their faces: lay face down in humility and appeal
decisions.reason: As in 14:5 and 16:4, 22, Moses and Aaron throw themselves down. Here they do it at the tent, turning to the LORD for help.

decisions.choice: the glory of the LORD appeared: the LORD's visible presence
decisions.reason: The glory appears at the tent, as it did when the people rebelled before (14:10; 16:19; 17:7). This time it comes with instructions for giving water, not with a judgment on the people.

decisions.choice: the crowd
decisions.reason: Readable calls the assembly "the crowd" here, since it is the angry gathering of verse 2.

decisions.choice: spoke to Moses: the word comes to Moses, but the task is shared
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks to Moses, but the command that follows includes Aaron (verse 8), and both are held responsible in verse 12.

source.text: קַ֣ח אֶת־הַמַּטֶּ֗ה וְהַקְהֵ֤ל אֶת־הָעֵדָה֙ אַתָּה֙ וְאַהֲרֹ֣ן אָחִ֔יךָ וְדִבַּרְתֶּ֧ם אֶל־הַסֶּ֛לַע לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם וְנָתַ֣ן מֵימָ֑יו וְהוֹצֵאתָ֨לָהֶ֥ם מַ֨יִם֙ מִן־הַסֶּ֔לַע וְהִשְׁקִיתָ֥ אֶת־הָעֵדָ֖ה וְאֶת־בְּעִירָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Take the staff and assemble the congregation, you and Aaron your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water; and you will bring out for them water from the rock and give drink to the congregation and their livestock.

en.L: "Take the staff, and assemble the congregation, you and Aaron your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water. And you will bring out water for them from the rock and give drink to the congregation and their livestock."
en.B: "Take the staff, and gather the congregation together, you and your brother Aaron. Then, while they watch, speak to the rock, and it will pour out its water. So you will bring water out of the rock for them and give the congregation and their animals something to drink."
en.R: "Take the staff. Then you and your brother Aaron must call the community together. While they are watching, speak to the rock, and water will pour out of it. In this way you will give the people and their animals water from the rock to drink."

es.L: «Toma la vara y reúne a la comunidad, tú y Aarón tu hermano, y {{plural_you:hablen|hablad}} a la peña ante sus ojos, y ella dará su agua. Y sacarás para ellos agua de la peña, y darás de beber a la comunidad y a su ganado».
es.B: «Toma la vara y reúne a la comunidad, tú y tu hermano Aarón. Luego, mientras ellos miran, {{plural_you:hablen|hablad}} a la peña, y ella dejará brotar su agua. Así sacarás agua de la peña para ellos y darás de beber a la comunidad y a sus animales».
es.R: «Toma la vara. Después, tú y tu hermano Aarón {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} que reunir a la comunidad. Mientras ellos miran, {{plural_you:hablen|hablad}} a la peña, y de ella saldrá agua en abundancia. Así darás a la gente y a sus animales agua de la peña para beber».

fr.L: « Prends le bâton, et rassemble la communauté, toi et Aaron ton frère, et parlez au rocher sous leurs yeux, et il donnera son eau. Et tu feras sortir pour eux de l’eau du rocher, et tu donneras à boire à la communauté et à leur bétail. »
fr.B: « Prends le bâton, et rassemble la communauté, toi et ton frère Aaron. Puis, sous leurs yeux, parlez au rocher, et il laissera jaillir son eau. Ainsi tu feras sortir pour eux de l’eau du rocher, et tu donneras à boire à la communauté et à ses bêtes. »
fr.R: « Prends le bâton. Puis, toi et ton frère Aaron, vous devez réunir la communauté. Pendant qu’ils regardent, parlez au rocher, et l’eau en sortira à flots. De cette façon, tu donneras à boire aux gens et à leurs animaux l’eau du rocher. »

sw.L: "Chukua fimbo, ukaikusanye jumuiya, wewe na Haruni ndugu yako, mkaseme na mwamba mbele ya macho yao, nao utatoa maji yake. Nawe utawatolea maji kutoka mwambani, na kuinywesha jumuiya pamoja na mifugo yao."
sw.B: "Chukua fimbo, ukaikusanye jumuiya, wewe na ndugu yako Haruni. Kisha, wakiwa wanatazama, semeni na mwamba, nao utatoa maji yake. Hivyo utawatolea maji kutoka mwambani, na kuinywesha jumuiya na wanyama wao."
sw.R: "Chukua fimbo. Kisha wewe na ndugu yako Haruni mwite jumuiya ikusanyike. Wakiwa wanatazama, semeni na mwamba, na maji yatabubujika kutoka ndani yake. Kwa njia hiyo utawapa watu na wanyama wao maji ya kunywa kutoka mwambani."

vi.L: "Hãy lấy cây gậy, và triệu tập hội chúng, ngươi và A-rôn anh ngươi, và hãy nói với tảng đá trước mắt họ, thì nó sẽ cho ra nước của nó. Và ngươi sẽ đem nước ra từ tảng đá cho họ và cho hội chúng cùng súc vật họ uống."
vi.B: "Hãy cầm cây gậy, rồi con và A-rôn, anh con, hãy tập họp hội chúng lại. Trước mắt họ, hãy nói với tảng đá, thì nó sẽ tuôn nước ra. Như vậy con sẽ làm cho nước từ tảng đá chảy ra cho họ, và cho hội chúng cùng súc vật họ uống."
vi.R: "Hãy cầm cây gậy. Rồi con và A-rôn, anh con, phải gọi cả cộng đồng lại. Trong khi họ đứng xem, hãy nói với tảng đá, rồi nước sẽ từ đó tuôn ra. Như vậy con sẽ cho dân chúng và súc vật của họ uống nước từ tảng đá."

decisions.choice: the staff: probably Aaron's staff kept before the LORD
alternatives: Moses' own staff, used in Egypt and at Rephidim
decisions.reason: The staff is taken "from before the LORD" (verse 9), where Aaron's staff that budded had been placed as a sign against rebels (17:25). But verse 11 calls it "his staff", Moses' own, which could point to the staff Moses carried in Egypt and at Rephidim (Exodus 4:20; 17:5). The text does not settle which staff is meant.

decisions.choice: speak to the rock: the command is to speak, not to strike
decisions.reason: At Rephidim the LORD told Moses to strike the rock (Exodus 17:6). Here he is told to speak to it in front of the people. What Moses does instead (verse 11) is the center of the story.

decisions.choice: the rock: a crag or cliff of rock
decisions.reason: The word here (sela') usually means a high rock or a cliff face. At Rephidim a different word for rock (tsur) is used (Exodus 17:6). Both mean rock; the change helps keep the two stories apart.

decisions.choice: your brother Aaron
decisions.reason: English puts "your brother" before the name; Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

decisions.choice: la peña
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word here (sela') is a crag or cliff of rock, not the word used at Rephidim (Exodus 17:6, "la roca"). "Peña" names a large rock face and keeps the two stories apart, as the meaning decision on this verse notes.

decisions.choice: parlez au rocher
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb "speak" is plural, for Moses and Aaron together, between singular commands to Moses; French shows it by moving from "tu" to "vous", as the Spanish and Swahili do.

decisions.choice: "A-rôn anh ngươi / anh con" (Aaron your brother)
decisions.reason: Aaron is the elder brother (Exodus 7:7), so Vietnamese, which must choose, says "anh", as the Vietnamese Exodus does.

fr.B: Moïse prit donc le bâton à sa place devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le lui avait ordonné.
fr.R: Moïse a donc pris le bâton à l’endroit où on le gardait, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le lui avait dit.

sw.L: Basi Musa akaichukua fimbo kutoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kama alivyomwamuru.
sw.B: Basi Musa akaichukua fimbo mahali ilipokuwa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kama alivyomwamuru.
sw.R: Basi Musa akaichukua fimbo pale ilipotunzwa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwambia.

vi.L: Và Môi-se lấy cây gậy từ trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã truyền cho ông.
vi.B: Vậy Môi-se lấy cây gậy từ chỗ của nó trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã truyền cho ông.
vi.R: Vậy Môi-se lấy cây gậy từ chỗ người ta cất nó trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã bảo ông.

decisions.choice: from before the LORD: from the tent, in front of the ark
decisions.reason: Things kept "before the LORD" were stored in the tent in front of the ark of the testimony, as Aaron's staff was (17:22, 25).

decisions.choice: as he had commanded him: Moses begins by obeying
decisions.reason: Up to this point Moses does exactly what he was told. The change comes in verses 10-11.

decisions.choice: from its place / from where it was kept
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add words to show that the staff had been kept in the LORD's presence, in the tent.

source.text: וַיַּקְהִ֜לוּ מֹשֶׁ֧ה וְאַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶת־הַקָּהָ֖ל אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַסָּ֑לַע וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם שִׁמְעוּ־נָא֙ הַמֹּרִ֔ים הֲמִן־הַסֶּ֣לַע הַזֶּ֔ה נוֹצִ֥יא לָכֶ֖ם מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And assembled Moses and Aaron the assembly before the rock, and he said to them, hear now, the rebels: from the rock the this will we bring out for you water?

en.L: And Moses and Aaron assembled the assembly before the rock, and he said to them, "Hear now, you rebels: from this rock will we bring out water for you?"
en.B: Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock, and Moses said to them, "Listen, you rebels! Are we to bring water out of this rock for you?"
en.R: Moses and Aaron called all the people together in front of the rock. Moses said to them, "Listen, you rebels! Are we supposed to get water for you out of this rock?"

es.L: Y reunieron Moisés y Aarón a la asamblea delante de la peña, y él les dijo: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} ahora, rebeldes: ¿de esta peña {{plural_you:les|os}} sacaremos agua?».
es.B: Moisés y Aarón reunieron a la asamblea delante de la peña, y Moisés les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, rebeldes! ¿Acaso {{plural_you:les|os}} tenemos que sacar agua de esta peña?».
es.R: Moisés y Aarón llamaron a todo el pueblo delante de la peña. Moisés les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, rebeldes! ¿Se supone que nosotros {{plural_you:les|os}} vamos a sacar agua de esta peña?».

fr.L: Et Moïse et Aaron rassemblèrent l’assemblée devant le rocher, et il leur dit : « Écoutez donc, rebelles : de ce rocher, vous ferons-nous sortir de l’eau ? »
fr.B: Moïse et Aaron réunirent l’assemblée devant le rocher, et Moïse leur dit : « Écoutez, rebelles ! Est-ce de ce rocher que nous devons faire sortir de l’eau pour vous ? »
fr.R: Moïse et Aaron ont appelé tout le peuple devant le rocher. Moïse leur a dit : « Écoutez, rebelles ! Est-ce que nous sommes censés vous faire sortir de l’eau de ce rocher ? »

sw.L: Kisha Musa na Haruni wakalikusanya kusanyiko mbele ya mwamba, naye akawaambia, "Sikieni basi, enyi waasi: je, tutawatolea maji kutoka katika mwamba huu?"
sw.B: Musa na Haruni walilikusanya kusanyiko mbele ya mwamba, naye Musa akawaambia, "Sikilizeni, enyi waasi! Je, ni lazima tuwatolee maji kutoka katika mwamba huu?"
sw.R: Musa na Haruni waliwaita watu wote mbele ya mwamba. Musa akawaambia, "Sikilizeni, ninyi waasi! Je, mnadhani sisi tutawatolea maji kutoka katika mwamba huu?"

vi.L: Và Môi-se và A-rôn tập họp hội lại trước tảng đá, và ông nói với họ: "Hãy nghe đây, hỡi những kẻ phản nghịch: chúng ta sẽ đem nước ra từ tảng đá này cho các ngươi sao?"
vi.B: Môi-se và A-rôn tập họp hội chúng trước tảng đá, và Môi-se nói với họ: "Hãy nghe đây, hỡi những kẻ phản nghịch! Chúng tôi phải làm cho nước từ tảng đá này chảy ra cho anh em sao?"
vi.R: Môi-se và A-rôn gọi cả dân chúng đến tụ họp trước tảng đá. Môi-se nói với họ: "Hãy nghe đây, những kẻ phản nghịch kia! Chúng tôi phải lấy nước từ tảng đá này ra cho anh em sao?"

decisions.choice: rebels: people who defy authority
decisions.reason: The word (morim) comes from the verb "rebel" that the LORD uses in verse 24, when he says that Moses and Aaron "rebelled against my command". The name Moses gives the people comes back on Moses and Aaron themselves.

decisions.choice: will we bring out water: a question that can be heard in more than one way
alternatives: an angry question: must we bring water for you?
a doubtful question: can we bring water out of this rock?
decisions.reason: The question may be angry ("must we?") or doubting ("can we?"). Either way Moses says "we", speaking of what he and Aaron will do, and does not name the LORD as the one who gives the water (verses 8, 12).

decisions.choice: Moses said
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he said". Moses is the speaker (verse 11 continues with him), so Balanced and Readable name him.

decisions.choice: Moses speaks to the people as "các ngươi" (Literal) and "anh em" (Balanced, Readable), and of himself and Aaron as "chúng ta" (Literal) / "chúng tôi" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet for Moses speaking to Israel. "chúng tôi" at Balanced and Readable leaves the people out of the "we", as Moses means himself and Aaron; Literal keeps the plainer "chúng ta". The question is left open, as the meaning decision's footnote asks.

records.literal_gloss: And lifted up Moses his hand and struck the rock with his staff twice, and came out water much, and drank the congregation and their livestock.

en.L: And Moses lifted up his hand and struck the rock with his staff two times, and much water came out, and the congregation drank, and their livestock.
en.B: Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water gushed out in abundance, and the congregation and their animals drank.
en.R: Then Moses raised his arm and hit the rock two times with his staff. A great amount of water poured out, and the people and their animals drank.

es.L: Y alzó Moisés su mano y golpeó la peña con su vara dos veces, y salió mucha agua, y bebió la comunidad y su ganado.
es.B: Entonces Moisés levantó la mano y golpeó la peña dos veces con su vara. El agua brotó en abundancia, y bebieron la comunidad y sus animales.
es.R: Entonces Moisés levantó el brazo y golpeó la peña dos veces con su vara. Salió muchísima agua, y la gente y sus animales bebieron.

fr.L: Et Moïse leva sa main et frappa le rocher avec son bâton, deux fois, et il sortit beaucoup d’eau, et la communauté but, ainsi que leur bétail.
fr.B: Alors Moïse leva la main et frappa deux fois le rocher avec son bâton. L’eau jaillit en abondance, et la communauté et ses bêtes burent.
fr.R: Alors Moïse a levé le bras et il a frappé le rocher deux fois avec son bâton. Beaucoup d’eau en est sortie, et les gens et leurs animaux ont bu.

sw.L: Kisha Musa akainua mkono wake, akaupiga mwamba kwa fimbo yake mara mbili, na maji mengi yakatoka, nayo jumuiya ikanywa, na mifugo yao.
sw.B: Ndipo Musa alipoinua mkono wake akaupiga mwamba mara mbili kwa fimbo yake. Maji yakabubujika kwa wingi, na jumuiya pamoja na wanyama wao wakanywa.
sw.R: Kisha Musa aliinua mkono wake, akaupiga mwamba mara mbili kwa fimbo yake. Maji mengi sana yakatoka, na watu na wanyama wao wakanywa.

vi.L: Và Môi-se giơ tay lên và lấy gậy mình đập vào tảng đá hai lần, và nước chảy ra rất nhiều, và hội chúng uống, cùng súc vật họ.
vi.B: Rồi Môi-se giơ tay lên và lấy gậy đập vào tảng đá hai lần. Nước tuôn ra dồi dào, và hội chúng cùng súc vật họ đều uống.
vi.R: Rồi Môi-se giơ cánh tay lên và lấy gậy đập vào tảng đá hai lần. Rất nhiều nước tuôn ra, và dân chúng cùng súc vật của họ uống.

decisions.choice: struck the rock twice: Moses does not do what he was told
decisions.reason: Moses was told to speak to the rock (verse 8). Instead he strikes it, and twice. The LORD still gives the water, plenty of it, but in verse 12 the LORD judges what Moses and Aaron did as a failure to trust him.

decisions.choice: his staff: the staff Moses took in verse 9
decisions.reason: "His staff" may simply be the staff in his hand, the one he took from before the LORD; see the note on verse 8.

decisions.choice: raised his arm
decisions.reason: Raising the hand here is lifting the arm to strike, so Readable says "arm".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹן֒ יַ֚עַן לֹא־הֶאֱמַנְתֶּ֣ם בִּ֔י לְהַ֨קְדִּישֵׁ֔נִי לְעֵינֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לָכֵ֗ן לֹ֤א תָבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶת־הַקָּהָ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה אֶל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תִּי לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses and to Aaron, because not you believed in me, to treat me as holy in [the] eyes of [the] sons of Israel, therefore not you will bring the assembly the this into the land that I have given to them.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and to Aaron, "Because you did not trust in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, to treat {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as holy before the eyes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, therefore you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given to them."
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron, "You did not trust {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and so you failed to show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holiness before the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. For that reason you will not be the ones to lead this assembly into the land I have given them."
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron, "You did not trust {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You did not show the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} that I am holy. So you will not lead these people into the land I have given them."

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Moisés y a Aarón: «Por cuanto no {{plural_you:confiaron|confiasteis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, de modo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:trataran|tratarais}} como santo ante los ojos de los hijos de Israel, por tanto no {{plural_you:introducirán|introduciréis}} esta asamblea en la tierra que les he dado».
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés y a Aarón: «No {{plural_you:confiaron|confiasteis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y así no {{plural_you:mostraron|mostrasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} santidad ante los israelitas. Por eso no {{plural_you:serán ustedes quienes conduzcan|seréis vosotros quienes conduzcáis}} a esta asamblea a la tierra que les he dado».
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les dijo a Moisés y a Aarón: «No {{plural_you:confiaron|confiasteis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. No les {{plural_you:mostraron|mostrasteis}} a los israelitas que yo soy santo. Por eso no {{plural_you:llevarán|llevaréis}} a este pueblo a la tierra que les he dado».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse et à Aaron : « Parce que vous n’avez pas eu foi en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, pour {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} traiter comme saint aux yeux des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, à cause de cela vous ne ferez pas entrer cette assemblée dans le pays que je leur ai donné. »
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse et à Aaron : « Vous ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez pas fait confiance, et ainsi vous n’avez pas montré {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} sainteté devant les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. C’est pourquoi ce n’est pas vous qui conduirez cette assemblée dans le pays que je leur ai donné. »
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse et à Aaron : « Vous ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez pas fait confiance. Vous n’avez pas montré aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} que je suis saint. Alors vous ne ferez pas entrer ce peuple dans le pays que je leur ai donné. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawaambia Musa na Haruni, "Kwa sababu hamkuniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, kunitakasa machoni pa wana wa Israeli, kwa hiyo hamtalileta kusanyiko hili katika nchi niliyowapa."
sw.B: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaambia Musa na Haruni, "Hamkuniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, na hivyo hamkuonyesha utakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mbele ya Waisraeli. Kwa sababu hiyo, si ninyi mtakaoliongoza kusanyiko hili kuingia katika nchi niliyowapa."
sw.R: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaambia Musa na Haruni, "Hamkuniamini. Hamkuwaonyesha Waisraeli kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni mtakatifu. Kwa hiyo hamtawaongoza watu hawa kuingia katika nchi niliyowapa."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se và A-rôn: "Vì các ngươi đã không tin cậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, để tôn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là thánh trước mắt con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, cho nên các ngươi sẽ không đem hội này vào xứ mà Ta đã ban cho họ."
vi.B: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se và A-rôn: "Các con đã không tin cậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nên đã không tỏ ra sự thánh khiết của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trước mặt dân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Vì thế các con sẽ không phải là người dẫn hội chúng này vào xứ Ta đã ban cho họ."
vi.R: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se và A-rôn: "Các con đã không tin cậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Các con đã không cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên thấy rằng Ta là thánh. Vì vậy các con sẽ không dẫn dân này vào xứ Ta đã ban cho họ."

decisions.choice: trust in me: rely on the LORD and take his word as sure
decisions.reason: The verb (he'emin) means to rely on someone and treat their word as certain. It is used when Abram trusted the LORD (Genesis 15:6) and when the people would not (14:11). Moses and Aaron did not act on the word the LORD had given.

decisions.choice: to treat me as holy: to show before the people that the LORD is holy
decisions.reason: To treat the LORD as holy here means to honor the LORD in public by doing exactly what was commanded, so that the people would see that the water came from the LORD. Scripture describes the failure in more than one way: as rebellion against the LORD's command (verse 24; 27:14) and as rash words from Moses' lips (Psalm 106:32-33).

decisions.choice: you will not bring this assembly into the land: Moses and Aaron are barred
decisions.reason: Moses and Aaron will lead the people to the edge of the land but not into it. Aaron dies at Mount Hor (verses 24-28), and Moses sees the land from a mountain before he dies (27:12-14; Deuteronomy 32:48-52; 34:4).

decisions.choice: two sentences in place of "because ... therefore"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the failure first and then its result, in separate sentences, instead of one long "because ... therefore" sentence.

decisions.choice: lead this assembly / lead these people
decisions.reason: "Bring" the assembly into the land means to lead them there; Balanced and Readable say "lead".

decisions.choice: God calls Moses and Aaron together "các ngươi" (Literal) and "các con" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The plural of the address God uses for Moses; it keeps the judgment personal rather than official.

source.text: הֵ֚מָּה מֵ֣י מְרִיבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־רָב֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּקָּדֵ֖שׁ בָּֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: They [are the] waters of Meribah, where quarreled [the] sons of Israel with Yahweh, and he showed himself holy among them.

en.L: These [are] the waters of Meribah, where the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel quarreled with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} holy among them.
en.B: These were the waters of Meribah, "quarreling," where the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} quarreled with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} holy among them.
en.R: This place was called the waters of Meribah, which means "arguing." There the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} argued with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed them that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is holy.

es.L: Estas [son] las aguas de Meribá, donde contendieron los hijos de Israel con {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se mostró santo entre ellos.
es.B: Estas fueron las aguas de Meribá, «Contienda», donde los israelitas contendieron con {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se mostró santo entre ellos.
es.R: Ese lugar se llamó las aguas de Meribá, que significa «discusión». Allí los israelitas discutieron con {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les mostró que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es santo.

fr.L: Ce [sont] les eaux de Meriba, où les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël cherchèrent querelle {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se montra saint parmi eux.
fr.B: Ce furent les eaux de Meriba, « Querelle », où les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} cherchèrent querelle {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, et où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se montra saint parmi eux.
fr.R: Ce lieu a été appelé les eaux de Meriba, ce qui veut dire « dispute ». Là, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} se sont disputés avec {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur a montré qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est saint.

sw.L: Haya [ndiyo] maji ya Meriba, ambapo wana wa Israeli waligombana na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akajionyesha mtakatifu kati yao.
sw.B: Haya ndiyo yaliyokuwa maji ya Meriba, "Ugomvi," ambapo Waisraeli waligombana na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akajionyesha mtakatifu kati yao.
sw.R: Mahali hapo paliitwa maji ya Meriba, maana yake "kubishana." Huko Waisraeli walibishana na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawaonyesha kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mtakatifu.

vi.L: Đây [là] nước Mê-ri-ba, nơi con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên cãi vã với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã tỏ mình là thánh giữa họ.
vi.B: Đó là nước Mê-ri-ba, nghĩa là "cãi vã", nơi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã cãi vã với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã tỏ mình là thánh giữa họ.
vi.R: Nơi này được gọi là nước Mê-ri-ba, nghĩa là "cãi nhau". Tại đó dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã cãi nhau với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã cho họ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là thánh.

decisions.choice: Meribah: "quarreling"
decisions.reason: The name comes from the verb "quarrel" used here and in verse 3. The same name was given at Rephidim (Exodus 17:7); this place is later called Meribah of Kadesh (27:14; Deuteronomy 32:51), which tells the two apart.

decisions.choice: showed himself holy: a play on the name Kadesh
decisions.reason: The verb (qadash, "be holy") sounds like Kadesh, "holy place", the name of the town (verse 1). Though Moses and Aaron did not treat the LORD as holy (verse 12), the LORD's holiness was shown, both in giving the water and in judging the leaders.

decisions.choice: quarreled with the LORD: the complaint was really against God
decisions.reason: The people quarreled with Moses (verse 3), but the verse says their quarrel was with the LORD, as Exodus 16:8 says of their grumbling.

decisions.choice: "quarreling" / which means "arguing"
decisions.reason: The point of the name is lost unless the reader knows what it means, so Balanced and Readable give its meaning, as at Exodus 17:7.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח מֹשֶׁ֧ה מַלְאָכִ֛ים מִקָּדֵ֖שׁ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ אֱד֑וֹם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אָחִ֣יךָ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַתְּלָאָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר מְצָאָֽתְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Moses messengers from Kadesh to [the] king of Edom: thus says your brother Israel, you know all the hardship that has found us.

en.L: And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: "Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the hardship that has found us.
en.B: From Kadesh Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom: "This is what your brother Israel says: You know about all the hardships we have been through.
en.R: While Israel was at Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom. They said, "Your brother Israel sends you this message: You know about all the troubles we have had.

vi.L: Và Môi-se sai sứ giả từ Ca-đe đến vua Ê-đôm: "Y-sơ-ra-ên, em của ông, nói thế này: Ông biết mọi gian khổ đã xảy đến cho chúng tôi.
vi.B: Từ Ca-đe, Môi-se sai sứ giả đến vua Ê-đôm mà nói: "Đây là lời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, em của ông: Ông biết mọi gian khổ chúng tôi đã trải qua.
vi.R: Khi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên ở Ca-đe, Môi-se sai sứ giả đến gặp vua Ê-đôm. Họ nói: "Y-sơ-ra-ên, em của ông, gửi đến ông lời này: Ông biết mọi khó khăn chúng tôi đã gặp.

decisions.choice: your brother Israel: Edom and Israel are related peoples
decisions.reason: Edom descended from Esau, the twin brother of Jacob, who was renamed Israel (Genesis 25:24-26; 32:29; 36:1). Moses appeals to this family bond. Deuteronomy 23:8 later tells Israel not to despise an Edomite, because he is a brother.

decisions.choice: messengers ... thus says: the form of a message sent by envoys
decisions.reason: "Thus says" opens a message carried by envoys in the sender's name. The messengers speak as Israel, in the first person ("we", "us").

decisions.choice: the hardship that has found us: the troubles that have worn us down
decisions.reason: The word (tela'ah) means weariness, the kind of trouble that wears a person out. It is used of what Israel suffered in Egypt and on the way (Exodus 18:8). Hardship "finding" someone means coming upon them.

decisions.choice: While Israel was at Kadesh / They said
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence and adds that the messengers spoke the message, so the reader can follow who is speaking.

decisions.choice: "Y-sơ-ra-ên, em của ông" (your brother Israel), with "ông" for the king
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say older or younger brother: Israel comes from Jacob, the younger twin of Esau, the father of Edom, so "em". The king is addressed as "ông", as the envoys address him in the Vietnamese Judges 11:17.

source.text: וַיֵּרְד֤וּ אֲבֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ מִצְרַ֔יְמָה וַנֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וַיָּרֵ֥עוּ לָ֛נוּ מִצְרַ֖יִם וְלַאֲבֹתֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went down our fathers to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt many days, and did evil to us Egypt and to our fathers.

en.L: And our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt many days, and Egypt did evil to us and to our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.
en.B: Our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} went down to Egypt, and we lived there a long time. The Egyptians mistreated us and our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.
en.R: Our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} went down to Egypt, and we lived there for many years. The Egyptians were cruel to us and to our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.

vi.L: Và tổ phụ chúng tôi đã đi xuống Ai Cập, và chúng tôi đã sống tại Ai Cập nhiều ngày, và Ai Cập đối xử ác với chúng tôi và với tổ phụ chúng tôi.
vi.B: Tổ phụ chúng tôi đã xuống Ai Cập, và chúng tôi sống ở đó lâu ngày. Người Ai Cập đã ngược đãi chúng tôi và tổ phụ chúng tôi.
vi.R: Tổ tiên chúng tôi đã xuống Ai Cập, và chúng tôi sống ở đó nhiều năm. Người Ai Cập đã đối xử tàn ác với chúng tôi và với tổ tiên chúng tôi.

decisions.choice: many days: a long time
decisions.reason: "Many days" means a long period, here the years of Israel's stay in Egypt (Exodus 12:40).

decisions.choice: we ... us and our fathers: Israel speaks as one people across the generations
decisions.reason: The message speaks as if the present generation lived in Egypt and suffered there along with their ancestors, because Israel is one people from Jacob's day to Moses'.

decisions.choice: Egypt: the people of Egypt
decisions.reason: The name of the country stands for its people, who did harm to Israel.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "Egypt" as the subject; Balanced and Readable name the people.

source.text: וַנִּצְעַ֤ק אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע קֹלֵ֔נוּ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָ֔ךְ וַיֹּצִאֵ֖נוּ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וְהִנֵּה֙ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ בְקָדֵ֔שׁ עִ֖יר קְצֵ֥ה גְבוּלֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And we cried out to Yahweh, and he heard our voice and sent [an] angel and brought us out from Egypt; and here we [are] in Kadesh, [a] city [at the] edge of your territory.

en.L: And we cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard our voice and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. And here we [are] in Kadesh, a city at the edge of your territory.
en.B: When we cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard our voice. He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are here at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your territory.
en.R: But we cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard us. He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are at Kadesh, a town at the edge of your land.

vi.L: Và chúng tôi đã kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nghe tiếng chúng tôi, sai một thiên sứ và đem chúng tôi ra khỏi Ai Cập. Và này, chúng tôi [đang ở] Ca-đe, một thành ở bờ cõi của ông.
vi.B: Khi chúng tôi kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nghe tiếng chúng tôi. Ngài sai một thiên sứ đem chúng tôi ra khỏi Ai Cập. Bây giờ chúng tôi đang ở Ca-đe, một thành ở ngay biên giới lãnh thổ của ông.
vi.R: Nhưng chúng tôi đã kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp đỡ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nghe chúng tôi. Ngài sai một thiên sứ đem chúng tôi ra khỏi Ai Cập. Bây giờ chúng tôi đang ở Ca-đe, một thành ở sát biên giới đất của ông.

decisions.choice: angel: a messenger sent by the LORD
decisions.reason: The word (mal'akh) means a messenger. Here it is the one sent by the LORD who went before Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 14:19; 23:20; 32:34). It is the same word as the "messengers" Moses sends in verse 14.

decisions.choice: we cried out ... he heard our voice: the exodus in brief
decisions.reason: The message retells the exodus in the words of Exodus 2:23-24 and 3:7-9: the cry of the oppressed, the LORD hearing it, and rescue. Israel tells a foreign king what the LORD has done.

decisions.choice: a city at the edge of your territory: Kadesh lay on Edom's border
decisions.reason: Kadesh stood near the western edge of the land Edom controlled, so the way east or north led through Edom's territory.

decisions.choice: for help
decisions.reason: Readable says why the people cried out, which the story of the exodus makes clear.

source.text: נַעְבְּרָה־נָּ֣א בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ לֹ֤א נַעֲבֹר֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה וּבְכֶ֔רֶם וְלֹ֥א נִשְׁתֶּ֖ה מֵ֣י בְאֵ֑ר דֶּ֧רֶךְ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ נֵלֵ֗ךְ לֹ֤א נִטֶּה֙ יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֔אול עַ֥ד אֲשֶֽׁר־נַעֲבֹ֖ר גְּבוּלֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Let us pass, please, through your land; not we will pass through field or through vineyard, and not we will drink water of a well. [The] way of the king we will go; not we will turn aside right or left until that we have passed through your territory.

en.L: Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or through vineyard, and we will not drink the water of a well. We will go [by] the way of the king; we will not turn aside [to the] right or [to the] left until we have passed through your territory."
en.B: Allow us, please, to cross your land. We will stay out of your fields and vineyards, and we will not drink from your wells. We will keep to the King's Highway, turning neither right nor left, until we are out of your territory."
en.R: Please let us travel through your country. We will not walk through your fields or vineyards, and we will not drink water from your wells. We will stay on the main road, the King's Highway. We will not leave it to go right or left until we have gone all the way through your land."

vi.L: Xin cho chúng tôi đi qua xứ của ông. Chúng tôi sẽ không đi qua ruộng hay qua vườn nho, và chúng tôi sẽ không uống nước giếng. Chúng tôi sẽ đi [theo] đường của vua; chúng tôi sẽ không rẽ [sang] phải hay [sang] trái cho đến khi chúng tôi đã đi qua khỏi lãnh thổ của ông."
vi.B: Xin ông cho chúng tôi đi ngang qua xứ ông. Chúng tôi sẽ không vào ruộng hay vườn nho của ông, cũng không uống nước giếng của ông. Chúng tôi sẽ đi theo Đường Cái của Vua, không rẽ sang phải hay sang trái, cho đến khi ra khỏi lãnh thổ của ông."
vi.R: Xin cho chúng tôi đi ngang qua đất nước của ông. Chúng tôi sẽ không đi vào ruộng hay vườn nho của ông. Chúng tôi sẽ không uống nước giếng của ông. Chúng tôi sẽ đi trên con đường chính, là Đường Cái của Vua. Chúng tôi sẽ không rời khỏi đường ấy để đi sang phải hay sang trái, cho đến khi đi qua hết đất của ông."

decisions.choice: the way of the king: a main public road
decisions.reason: The "way of the king" was a main route through the highlands east of the Dead Sea, running north through Edom and Moab (21:22). It was a public road, and keeping to it meant not touching the land beside it.

decisions.choice: not drink the water of a well: not using Edom's water
decisions.reason: In dry country a well was precious property. Israel promises not to draw on Edom's wells, and offers to pay for any water it does use (verse 19).

decisions.choice: not turn aside right or left: not leave the road at all
decisions.reason: The phrase means keeping strictly to the way, without straying from it in any direction.

decisions.choice: the King's Highway
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the road its familiar name; Literal keeps "the way of the king". Readable also explains it as the main road.

decisions.choice: "Đường Cái của Vua" (the King's Highway), capitalised as a road's name
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable name the road; Vietnamese capitalises it the same way. Literal keeps "đường của vua". Used again in 21:22.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אֱד֔וֹם לֹ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר בִּ֑י פֶּן־בַּחֶ֖רֶב אֵצֵ֥א לִקְרָאתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Edom, not you will pass through me, lest with the sword I come out to meet you.

en.L: And Edom said to him, "You will not pass through me, or I will come out with the sword to meet you."
en.B: But Edom answered, "You will not cross our land. If you try, we will march out against you with the sword."
en.R: But Edom answered, "You may not go through our country. If you try, we will come out and attack you with our swords!"

vi.L: Và Ê-đôm nói với người: "Ngươi sẽ không đi qua [xứ] ta, kẻo ta sẽ đem gươm ra đón đánh ngươi."
vi.B: Nhưng Ê-đôm trả lời: "Các người không được đi qua xứ chúng ta. Nếu các người cố đi, chúng ta sẽ đem gươm ra đánh các người."
vi.R: Nhưng Ê-đôm trả lời: "Các người không được đi qua đất nước chúng ta. Nếu các người cố đi, chúng ta sẽ đem gươm ra tấn công các người!"

decisions.choice: Edom ... me ... I: the nation speaks as one person
decisions.reason: Edom answers in the singular, as Israel does in its messages (verses 14, 19). The nation speaks through its king.

decisions.choice: come out to meet you with the sword: go to war against you
decisions.reason: To "come out to meet" someone with the sword is to march out and fight them.

decisions.choice: our land / we
decisions.reason: English does not let a nation speak as "I", so Balanced and Readable say "we" and "our land". Literal keeps "me" and "I".

decisions.choice: Edom speaks to Israel as "ngươi / ta" (Literal) and "các người / chúng ta" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: A refusal and a threat: Vietnamese "các người" is cold and distant, unlike Israel's polite "ông". Literal keeps the Hebrew singular of the nation speaking as one person.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֥יו בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֘לבַּֽמְסִלָּ֣ה נַעֲלֶה֒ וְאִם־מֵימֶ֤יךָ נִשְׁתֶּה֙ אֲנִ֣י וּמִקְנַ֔י וְנָתַתִּ֖י מִכְרָ֑ם רַ֥ק אֵין־דָּבָ֖ר בְּרַגְלַ֥י אֶֽעֱבֹֽרָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him [the] sons of Israel, by the highway we will go up, and if your water we drink, I and my livestock, then I will give their price; only [there is] nothing, on my feet let me pass through.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel said to him, "We will go up by the highway, and if we drink your water, I and my livestock, then I will give its price. Only, [it is] nothing; let me pass through on my feet."
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} replied, "We will go up by the highway, and if we or our herds drink your water, we will pay its price. It is a small thing; all we ask is to cross on foot."
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} answered, "We will keep to the main road. If we or our animals drink any of your water, we will pay for it. We are not asking much. We just want to walk through your land."

vi.L: Và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên nói với người: "Chúng tôi sẽ đi lên theo đường cái, và nếu chúng tôi uống nước của ông, tôi và súc vật tôi, thì tôi sẽ trả giá nó. Chỉ [là] không có gì; xin cho tôi đi bộ qua thôi."
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đáp: "Chúng tôi sẽ đi theo đường cái, và nếu chúng tôi hay súc vật chúng tôi uống nước của ông, chúng tôi sẽ trả tiền. Đó là việc nhỏ; chúng tôi chỉ xin đi bộ ngang qua thôi."
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên trả lời: "Chúng tôi sẽ đi trên con đường chính. Nếu chúng tôi hay súc vật của chúng tôi uống chút nước nào của ông, chúng tôi sẽ trả tiền. Chúng tôi không xin gì nhiều. Chúng tôi chỉ muốn đi bộ ngang qua đất của ông."

decisions.choice: highway: a built-up road
decisions.reason: The word (mesillah) means a raised, prepared road, here the King's Highway of verse 17.

decisions.choice: only, there is nothing: it is no great matter
decisions.reason: The short phrase probably means "it is nothing", a small request. It could also mean "we want nothing else"; either way Israel stresses how little it asks.

decisions.choice: on my feet let me pass through: only to travel through on foot
decisions.reason: Israel asks only to walk through, not to stay, take land or make war.

decisions.choice: we / our
decisions.reason: The Israelites speak as one person ("I", "my"). Balanced and Readable say "we" and "our", as in verse 18; Literal keeps the Hebrew.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֹ֣א תַעֲבֹ֑ר וַיֵּצֵ֤א אֱדוֹם֙ לִקְרָאת֔וֹ בְּעַ֥ם כָּבֵ֖ד וּבְיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, not you will pass through. And came out Edom to meet him with people heavy and with hand strong.

en.L: And he said, "You will not pass through." And Edom came out to meet him with a heavy people and with a strong hand.
en.B: But Edom said, "You will not pass through." And Edom came out against them with a large army and a strong force.
en.R: But Edom said again, "You may not go through!" Then the Edomites came out to fight Israel with a large and powerful army.

vi.L: Và người nói: "Ngươi sẽ không đi qua." Và Ê-đôm kéo ra đón đánh người với dân đông đảo và với tay mạnh mẽ.
vi.B: Nhưng Ê-đôm nói: "Các người không được đi qua." Rồi Ê-đôm kéo ra chống lại họ với một đạo quân đông đảo và hùng mạnh.
vi.R: Nhưng Ê-đôm lại nói: "Các người không được đi qua!" Rồi người Ê-đôm kéo ra đánh Y-sơ-ra-ên với một đạo quân đông và mạnh.

decisions.choice: a heavy people and a strong hand: a large and powerful army
decisions.reason: "People" here means fighting men, and "heavy" means many. A "strong hand" is force, power used against someone.

decisions.choice: to meet him: to confront Israel
decisions.reason: "Him" is Israel, spoken of as one person. "Meet" here means to confront in battle, as in verse 18.

decisions.choice: Edom said / them / Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he said" and "him". Balanced and Readable name Edom as the speaker, and say "them" or "Israel" for the people Edom came out against.

source.text: וַיְמָאֵ֣ן׀אֱד֗וֹם נְתֹן֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֲבֹ֖ר בִּגְבֻל֑וֹ וַיֵּ֥ט יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעָלָֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And refused Edom to give Israel to pass through its territory, and turned aside Israel from upon it.

en.L: And Edom refused to let Israel pass through its territory, and Israel turned aside from it.
en.B: So Edom refused to let Israel pass through its territory, and Israel turned away from them.
en.R: Edom would not let Israel pass through its land, so Israel went another way.

vi.L: Và Ê-đôm từ chối cho Y-sơ-ra-ên đi qua lãnh thổ mình, và Y-sơ-ra-ên rẽ đi khỏi nó.
vi.B: Vậy Ê-đôm không chịu cho Y-sơ-ra-ên đi qua lãnh thổ mình, và Y-sơ-ra-ên quay đi nơi khác.
vi.R: Ê-đôm không cho Y-sơ-ra-ên đi qua đất của họ, nên Y-sơ-ra-ên đi đường khác.

decisions.choice: Israel turned aside: Israel does not fight Edom
decisions.reason: Israel does not force its way through. Deuteronomy 2:4-6 says the LORD told Israel not to fight Edom, the descendants of Esau, because their land was not given to Israel. Israel goes around Edom instead (21:4).

decisions.choice: to give Israel to pass: to allow Israel to pass
decisions.reason: "Give" with another verb means to let or allow.

decisions.choice: went another way
decisions.reason: "Turned aside from it" means Israel took a different route; Readable says so.

source.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִקָּדֵ֑שׁ וַיָּבֹ֧אוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל כָּל־הָעֵדָ֖ה הֹ֥ר הָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from Kadesh, and came [the] sons of Israel, all the congregation, [to] Hor the mountain.

en.L: And they set out from Kadesh, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, the whole congregation, came [to] Hor the mountain.
en.B: They set out from Kadesh, and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, the whole congregation, came to Mount Hor.
en.R: The whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.

vi.L: Và họ nhổ trại từ Ca-đe, và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, toàn thể hội chúng, đến núi Hô-rơ.
vi.B: Họ nhổ trại rời Ca-đe, và dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, toàn thể hội chúng, đến núi Hô-rơ.
vi.R: Toàn thể cộng đồng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên rời Ca-đe và đến núi Hô-rơ.

decisions.choice: Hor the mountain: a mountain on Edom's border
decisions.reason: Mount Hor is described as being on the border of the land of Edom (verse 23; 33:37). Its exact location is not known.

decisions.choice: Mount Hor
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, "Hor the mountain"; Balanced and Readable use the usual English form of a mountain's name.

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses and to Aaron at Hor the mountain, on [the] border of [the] land of Edom, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and to Aaron at Hor the mountain, on the border of the land of Edom, saying,
en.B: At Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron,
en.R: At Mount Hor, near the border of Edom, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron,

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se và A-rôn tại núi Hô-rơ, ở biên giới xứ Ê-đôm, rằng:
vi.B: Tại núi Hô-rơ, ở biên giới xứ Ê-đôm, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se và A-rôn:
vi.R: Tại núi Hô-rơ, gần biên giới Ê-đôm, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se và A-rôn:

decisions.choice: on the border of the land of Edom: Israel goes around Edom
decisions.reason: The place shows Israel moving along the edge of Edom's land rather than through it (verse 21).

decisions.choice: the place first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the place at the start of the sentence, so that the words of the LORD follow straight after "said".

source.text: יֵאָסֵ֤ף אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־עַמָּ֔יו כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָבֹא֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־מְרִיתֶ֥ם אֶת־פִּ֖י לְמֵ֥י מְרִיבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Will be gathered Aaron to his peoples, for not he will enter into the land that I have given to [the] sons of Israel, because that you rebelled against my mouth at [the] waters of Meribah.

en.L: "Aaron will be gathered to his peoples, for he will not enter the land that I have given to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, because you rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth at the waters of Meribah.
en.B: "Aaron is about to be gathered to his people. He will not enter the land I have given to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, because you both rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} command at the waters of Meribah.
en.R: "Aaron is going to die and join his ancestors. He will not go into the land I have given to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, because the two of you disobeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} command at the waters of Meribah.

vi.L: "A-rôn sẽ được về với dân mình, vì người sẽ không vào xứ mà Ta đã ban cho con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, bởi vì các ngươi đã chống lại miệng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tại nước Mê-ri-ba.
vi.B: "A-rôn sắp được về với tổ tông mình. Người sẽ không vào xứ Ta đã ban cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, vì cả hai con đã chống lại mạng lệnh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tại nước Mê-ri-ba.
vi.R: "A-rôn sắp qua đời và về với tổ tiên. Người sẽ không vào xứ Ta đã ban cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, vì cả hai con đã không vâng theo mạng lệnh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tại nước Mê-ri-ba.

decisions.choice: gathered to his people: to die and join those who died before
decisions.reason: The phrase is used only of death (Genesis 25:8; 49:33; Deuteronomy 32:50). It speaks of joining one's family in death, and is distinct from burial. "Peoples" is plural in the Hebrew, meaning one's kin. Aaron's death follows in verse 28.

decisions.choice: rebelled against my mouth: disobeyed my command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what is spoken, a command. The verb is from the root of "rebels", the word Moses used of the people (verse 10).

decisions.choice: you rebelled: Moses and Aaron together
decisions.reason: "You" is plural. Both brothers are held responsible for what happened at Meribah (verse 12).

decisions.choice: you both / the two of you
decisions.reason: English "you" does not show the plural, so Balanced and Readable make it clear that both Moses and Aaron are meant.

decisions.choice: die and join his ancestors
decisions.reason: Readable says what "gathered to his people" means, as at Genesis 25:8.

decisions.choice: "được về với dân mình" (Literal), "được về với tổ tông mình" (Balanced), "qua đời và về với tổ tiên" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The idiom as the Vietnamese Genesis 25:8 renders it ("về với tổ tông"); Literal keeps the Hebrew "his peoples". Used again in 20:26.

source.text: קַ֚ח אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹ֔ן וְאֶת־אֶלְעָזָ֖ר בְּנ֑וֹ וְהַ֥עַל אֹתָ֖ם הֹ֥ר הָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Take Aaron and Eleazar his son and bring them up [to] Hor the mountain.

en.L: Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up [on] Hor the mountain.
en.B: Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor.
en.R: Take Aaron and his son Eleazar up Mount Hor.

vi.L: Hãy đem A-rôn và Ê-lê-a-sa con trai người, và đưa họ lên núi Hô-rơ.
vi.B: Hãy đem A-rôn và Ê-lê-a-sa, con trai người, lên núi Hô-rơ.
vi.R: Hãy dẫn A-rôn và Ê-lê-a-sa, con trai người, lên núi Hô-rơ.

decisions.choice: Eleazar his son: the next high priest
decisions.reason: Eleazar was Aaron's third son (3:2) and already served as chief over the leaders of the Levites (3:32; 17:2). His older brothers Nadab and Abihu had died before the LORD (3:4).

decisions.choice: his son Eleazar
decisions.reason: English puts "his son" before the name; Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

source.text: וְהַפְשֵׁ֤ט אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶת־בְּגָדָ֔יו וְהִלְבַּשְׁתָּ֖ם אֶת־אֶלְעָזָ֣ר בְּנ֑וֹ וְאַהֲרֹ֥ן יֵאָסֵ֖ף וּמֵ֥ת שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And strip Aaron [of] his garments and clothe [with] them Eleazar his son, and Aaron will be gathered and will die there.

en.L: And strip Aaron [of] his garments and clothe Eleazar his son [with] them, and Aaron will be gathered and will die there."
en.B: Remove Aaron's garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people and die there."
en.R: Take off Aaron's priestly clothes and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will die there."

vi.L: Và hãy cởi áo xống của A-rôn và mặc [chúng] cho Ê-lê-a-sa con trai người, và A-rôn sẽ được về [với dân mình] và chết tại đó."
vi.B: Hãy cởi bộ áo của A-rôn và mặc cho Ê-lê-a-sa, con trai người. A-rôn sẽ được về với tổ tông và qua đời tại đó."
vi.R: Hãy cởi bộ áo thầy tế lễ của A-rôn ra và mặc cho Ê-lê-a-sa, con trai người. A-rôn sẽ qua đời tại đó."

decisions.choice: his garments: the holy garments of the high priest
decisions.reason: These are the holy garments made for Aaron as high priest (Exodus 28:2-4). Exodus 29:29-30 says they were to pass to his sons, who would be anointed and ordained in them. Putting them on Eleazar makes him high priest in his father's place.

decisions.choice: will be gathered: short for "gathered to his people"
decisions.reason: The verb stands alone here, but it means the same as the full phrase in verse 24.

decisions.choice: gathered to his people / priestly clothes
decisions.reason: Balanced completes the short phrase "will be gathered" from verse 24. Readable says "priestly clothes" so the reader knows which garments are meant, and since "will die" says the same thing, it gives only that.

decisions.reason: This time the command is carried out exactly, even though it means losing his brother.

decisions.reason: The whole people watch Aaron go up the mountain, so the handing on of the high priesthood is public.

decisions.choice: Aaron died there: in the fortieth year, at 123
decisions.reason: Numbers 33:38-39 gives the date, the first day of the fifth month of the fortieth year after the exodus, and Aaron's age, 123 years. Deuteronomy 10:6 names the place where Aaron died Moserah, which may be the name of the area around the mountain or of a camp near it.

decisions.choice: Moses and Eleazar came down: the priesthood goes on
decisions.reason: Three went up and two come down. Eleazar returns wearing the high priest's garments, so Aaron's office continues though Aaron is gone.

decisions.choice: priestly clothes
decisions.reason: As in verse 26, Readable says which garments are meant.

en.B: When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel mourned for him thirty days.
en.R: When all the people saw that Aaron was dead, the whole nation of Israel mourned for him for thirty days.

vi.L: Và toàn thể hội chúng thấy rằng A-rôn đã qua đời, và cả nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên khóc A-rôn ba mươi ngày.
vi.B: Khi toàn thể hội chúng thấy A-rôn đã qua đời, cả nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên để tang ông ba mươi ngày.
vi.R: Khi cả dân chúng biết A-rôn đã chết, toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên để tang ông ba mươi ngày.

decisions.choice: wept thirty days: a long, formal mourning
decisions.reason: A usual time of mourning was seven days (Genesis 50:10). Thirty days marks special honor, and Moses is mourned for the same length of time (Deuteronomy 34:8).

decisions.choice: the house of Israel: the whole people
decisions.reason: "House" here means the whole family descended from Israel, the nation.

decisions.choice: saw that Aaron had died: the people learn it when he does not come down
decisions.reason: The people see Moses and Eleazar come down without Aaron (verse 28), and Eleazar in his father's garments, and so they know that Aaron is dead.

decisions.choice: mourned
decisions.reason: "Wept" here names the formal weeping of mourning, so Balanced and Readable say "mourned"; Literal keeps "wept".
